item.title: MLB roundup: Pete Crow-Armstrong (3 HRs), Cubs overpower Reds
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong recorded his first three-homer game and drove in six runs to power the host Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pete Crow-Armstrong recorded his first three-homer game and drove in six runs to power the host Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday. Crow-Armstrong increased his team-leading homer total to 36 with a solo shot in the first inning, a two-run blast in the second and a three-run homer in the seventh. Carson Kelly added a three-run homer and an RBI double for Chicago. Seiya Suzuki belted a two-run homer while Alex Bregman also went deep and added an RBI single as both players finished with three hits. Tyrone Taylor matched Crow-Armstrong with four of the Cubs' 19 hits and Nico Hoerner added an RBI single to help the team snap a three-game losing skid. The power display backed Kevin Gausman (8-11), who allowed five runs on six hits in five innings. Cincinnati rookie Sal Stewart belted a two-run shot for his team-leading 30th homer of the season. Eugenio Suarez also had a two-run homer and JJ Bleday added a sacrifice fly for the Reds, who lost for the 10th time in 15 games. Red Sox 6, Yankees 0 (Game 1) Rookie Jake Bennett pitched six strong innings and visiting Boston piled on during a four-run ninth inning against New York. Bennett (9-6) allowed three hits in his fourth career scoreless start. He struck out seven without a walk and has allowed one run on six hits in 12 1/3 innings during his two starts against the Yankees. Wilyer Abreu homered in the first inning against New York starter Carlos Rodon (4-3), Adley Rutschman enjoyed his first three-hit game with the Red Sox and Andruw Monasterio added a two-run double to lead Boston. Yankees 9, Red Sox 2 (Game 2) Ben Rice capped New York's five-run eighth inning with a two-run single during a three-RBI night as it evened the season series with a doubleheader split against visiting Boston. The Yankees had seven hits in the eighth and 13 in the game after totaling just seven across the first two games of the series. New York actually took control during a three-run third inning off Brayan Bello (5-7). With the win, the Yankees moved three games ahead of the Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot. New York starter Max Fried held Boston to one run on three hits in 3 2/3 innings in his return from the injured list due to a bone bruise in his left elbow. Mets 6, Astros 2 Nolan McLean tossed seven innings of two-hit ball and earned the win for host New York, which beat Houston in the middle contest of a three-game interleague series. Juan Soto returned from the injured list after sitting out five weeks due to strained left calf and went 1-for-4 with the tiebreaking RBI single in the fifth for the Mets. Jared Young had three hits and three RBIs, including a two-run triple to close out the fifth-inning rally, as New York improved to 14-11 this month. Yordan Alvarez homered and had a sacrifice fly for the American League West-leading Astros, who fell to 3-2 on their New York road trip. White Sox 3, Twins 2 Andrew Benintendi went 3-for-4 with a double, a homer and two RBIs in Minneapolis as Chicago extended its win streak to four games. Benintendi's three hits marked the only hits of the day for the White Sox. Josh Bell and Walker Jenkins each went 1-for-3 with an RBI for the Twins and Luke Keaschall added a double. Chicago right-hander Erick Fedde (7-8) earned the win after holding Minnesota to two runs on three hits in five innings. Jenkins notched his first career RBI on a groundout in the second inning. Tigers 2, Dodgers 1 Kevin McGonigle delivered a bases-loaded single in the ninth to drive in the winning run as host Detroit edged Los Angeles to even their three-game series. Javier Baez scored both runs for the Tigers, who had lost eight of their previous nine games. Gleyber Torres drove in the other run for Detroit. Kenley Jansen (4-5) picked up the win in relief. Starter Keider Montero gave up one run and four hits in 5 1/3 innings. Freddie Freeman drove in the lone run as the Dodgers lost for the fourth time in five games. The loss spoiled a strong outing by starter Blake Snell, who gave up one run and three hits in five innings while striking out 10. Nationals 5, Marlins 4 (10 innings) Dylan Crews' two-out bases-loaded single in the 10th lifted host Washington to its first walk-off win of the season. Crews lined an 0-1 four-seam fastball from Michael Petersen (3-4) into right-center field for his first career walk-off hit. Heriberto Hernandez homered for Miami, which has lost four of its last five. Nationals starter Cade Cavalli left the game after taking a liner off his right calf with two out in the fourth. He recovered to throw Javier Sanoja out at first to end the half inning but limped to the dugout. Braves 2, Rockies 1 Michael Harris II laced a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth inning to help streaking Atlanta top visiting Colorado for its sixth straight win. Brent Suter (2-2) threw 2 1/3 scoreless innings for the Braves, while Jaden Hill (0-3) took the loss after allowing Harris' double among three hits in his one-inning relief appearance. Willi Castro plated the Rockies' lone run on a two-out run-scoring single in the sixth. Colorado's Ryan Feltner was scratched from his scheduled start due to illness. Blue Jays 4, Mariners 3 Alejandro Kirk singled in the go-ahead run in a two-run sixth, Jose Soriano pitched seven effective innings and host Toronto defeated Seattle. Soriano (11-7) allowed three runs, five hits and two walks while striking out six. Louis Varland pitched the ninth to earn his 31st save. Cal Raleigh hit a solo home run for the Mariners, who led 3-0 after four innings. The Blue Jays took a 4-3 lead in the sixth against Jose Ferrer (4-3). Charles McAdoo and Myles Straw walked. Brett Bateman grounded an RBI single with two outs that found a hole through the left side of the infield. Kirk's single to right scored the go-ahead run. Pirates 6, Cardinals 2 Rookie slugger Rafael Flores Jr. hit a three-run home run for visiting Pittsburgh, which effectively used six pitchers in a bullpen game to beat St. Louis and even their three-game series. Brandon Lowe added a solo homer in the first inning for the Pirates, who overcame three straight errors at one point in the game. Right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski (7-6) earned the victory by allowing an unearned run and one hit in 3 1/3 relief innings. Jacob Gonzalez hit a tie-breaking RBI single in the fourth and Flores made it 5-1 with two outs in the fifth with his seventh homer of the season off left-hander Brycen Mautz (0-1). Diamondbacks 7, Giants 1 (Game 1) Merrill Kelly combined with two relievers on a four-hitter, Lars Nootbaar broke a scoreless deadlock with a seventh-inning, pinch-hit grand slam and Arizona beat San Francisco in the opener of a day-night doubleheader. Kelly (9-12) called it a day after seven shutout innings in which he allowed just a pair of singles and four walks. The right-hander struck out seven. Brandyn Garcia wrapped up the Diamondbacks' seventh win in their last 10 games with a 1-2-3 ninth. Making his third big-league start, Giants rookie left-hander Matt Wilkinson (0-2) was charged with two of the runs. He limited Arizona to three hits in his six-plus innings, with two walks and four strikeouts. Giants 7, Diamondbacks 2 (Game 2) Bryce Eldridge matched career highs with four hits and four RBIs, Rafael Devers drove in two runs with a pair of singles, and host San Francisco salvaged a doubleheader split with Arizona in the nightcap. Making his major league debut after a promotion from Double-A Richmond, Giants right-hander Yunior Marte worked 4 2/3 innings, limiting the Diamondbacks to one run and three hits. Reiver Sanmartin (2-0), who relieved Marte with two outs in the fifth with the game tied at 1-1, was credited with the win after facing just one batter, striking out Game 1 hero Lars Nootbaar. Arizona rookie left-hander Mitch Bratt (1-3) was charged with three runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings. Royals 8, Guardians 3 Josh Rojas hit a two-run homer and tied his career high with four RBIs as surging Kansas City scored eight unanswered runs to beat host Cleveland and clinch a series win. Rojas had a two-run single in the sixth inning and added a two-run homer in the eighth to lift the Royals to their 12th win in 13 games. Royals reliever Anthony Gose (1-0) retired all five batters he faced to collect his first victory since June 17, 2022, while pitching for the Guardians. Cleveland reliever Colin Holderman (6-4) took the loss after recording only one out. He was charged with four runs (three earned) during Kansas City's breakout sixth. Angel Martinez had a two-run homer off starter Daniel Lynch IV for the Guardians. Rays 7, Padres 6 Chandler Simpson slashed a tiebreaking, two-out single to cap a four-run, seventh-inning rally, lifting Tampa Bay to a wild win and a series victory over San Diego in St. Petersburg, Fla. The Rays' Jonathan Aranda hit a tape-measure home run, and Junior Caminero ripped his 36th to tie Houston's Yordan Alvarez for the American League lead. Starting pitcher Nick Martinez allowed three runs on seven hits in six innings with four strikeouts and no walks. Reliever Kevin Kelly (6-3) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings, while Bryan Baker recorded his 39th save. The Padres' Dustin Harris had three hits, two runs and a stolen base. Ty France had two hits, including his 100th career homer. Manny Machado had two hits and two RBIs. Bradgley Rodriguez (3-3) allowed four runs (one earned) on three hits and a walk without retiring a batter. Orioles 5, Athletics 3 Leody Taveras doubled twice and drove in three runs as Baltimore downed the Athletics in West Sacramento, Calif. Colton Cowser homered and scored two runs in the second game of the three-game series and Coby Mayo also scored twice for the Orioles. Right-hander Shane Baz (5-14) ended a five-start losing streak by limiting the Athletics to two runs and five hits over 5 2/3 innings. He struck out four and walked three. Seeking his second straight win, A's starter Jack Perkins (3-10) limited Baltimore to two runs (one earned) and four hits over five innings. The right-hander struck out five and walked four. Carlos Cortes had two hits and an RBI, and Jeff McNeil had two hits and scored a run for the A's. Brewers 5, Rangers 3 Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning and Shane Drohan tossed five solid innings for host Milwaukee, which beat Texas for its fourth straight win. Drohan (7-5) allowed one run on six hits with one walk and six strikeouts for his first victory since July 31. Luis Lara had two hits and two RBIs for Milwaukee, which won its fourth straight. Brandon Nimmo hit a two-run homer as part of a three-hit game for the Rangers, and teammate Cody Freeman went deep for the first time this season. Phillies 4, Angels 2 (10 innings) Kyle Schwarber drove in the go-ahead run with a bloop double and Trea Turner added a two-run single to highlight a three-run 10th inning and lead Philadelphia over Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif. Alec Bohm went 2-for-4 with a run scored and Turner had two hits and two RBIs for Philadelphia, which won for the 12th time in its last 14 games. Jhoan Duran (2-4) picked up the win, allowing one unearned run in two innings of relief. Zach Neto hit a home run for Los Angeles, which finished with just four hits while losing its sixth straight game. Right-hander Trevor Martin (0-1), making his Angels debut after being claimed on waivers from Tampa Bay on Aug. 15, picked up the loss. --Field Level Media

item.title: Zambian opposition leader Mundubile charged with treason, lawyer says
item.description: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile was charged with treason on Saturday, his lawyer told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile was charged with treason on Saturday, his lawyer told Reuters. "Mr Brian Mundubile and his running mate, Mr Makebi Zulu, were both charged with treason and remained detained at Lusaka Central Police Station as of last night," lawyer Kambwa Aongola said. This follows his [USN:S8N3ZF05A TEXT:"arrest"] on Thursday after being questioned by police "in connection with an alleged offence of treason".

item.title: 'Words simply fall short': Inter Miami interim coach marvels at Messi masterclass
item.description: Inter Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos ran out of superlatives for Lionel Messi after the Argentine playmaker scored four goals in a Major League Soccer match for the first time in his career to inspire a 7-1 thrashing of CF Montreal on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Inter Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos ran out of superlatives for Lionel Messi after the Argentine playmaker scored four goals in a Major League Soccer match for the first time in his career to inspire a 7-1 thrashing of CF Montreal on Saturday. Messi's four-goal haul and an assist came at a crucial time for Miami, helping them snap a five-game winless run across all competitions. The 39-year-old restored Miami's advantage shortly before halftime, struck again in the 52nd minute, completed his hat-trick in the 83rd and capped his dazzling display with a free kick in stoppage time. The former Barcelona forward now tops the MLS scoring charts with 18 goals this season. "There are no words to describe such footballing beauty," Argentine Hoyos said. "So much is going on that words simply fall short. "He is constantly looking for that goal, that play, that pass; I don't think he's an ordinary footballer. Analysing him, both as a player and as a person, goes so deep that you run out of words." Messi, who won the 2022 World Cup, also captained Argentina to this year's World Cup final, where they lost to Spain. "That's what it means to have Messi on the team," Miami midfielder Casemiro told Apple TV. "We have to enjoy these moments because he is a person, a player that makes history." Casemiro, 34, joined Miami in July after his contract expired at Manchester United. The Brazilian and Messi spent years on opposite sides of one of football's fiercest rivalries, with Casemiro starring for Real Madrid and Messi for Barcelona, but are now teammates. "We saw today that we have to enjoy it, keep supporting and keep competing with him because he continues to be the best," Casemiro added. "He proved it in the World Cup. We have to enjoy it because, with him, we are so much stronger."

item.title: Phillies score 3 runs in 10th, hold off Angels
item.description: Kyle Schwarber drove in the go-ahead run with a bloop double and Trea Turner added a two-run single to highlight a three-run 10th inning and lead the Philadelphia Phillies to a 4-2 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Saturday night in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Schwarber drove in the go-ahead run with a bloop double and Trea Turner added a two-run single to highlight a three-run 10th inning and lead the Philadelphia Phillies to a 4-2 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Saturday night in Anaheim, Calif. Alec Bohm went 2-for-4 with a run scored and Turner had two hits and two RBIs for Philadelphia, which won for the 12th time in its last 14 games. Jhoan Duran (2-4) picked up the win, allowing one unearned run on one hit and one walk in two innings of relief. Zach Neto hit a home run for Los Angeles, which finished with just four hits while losing its sixth straight game. Right-hander Trevor Martin (0-1), making his Angels debut after being claimed on waivers from Tampa Bay on Aug. 15, picked up the loss, allowing three runs (two earned) on four hits and two walks in three innings. Philadelphia took a 1-0 lead in the second inning when Bohm led off with a single, advanced to second on a walk to Bryson Stott and scored on a single to center by Brandon Marsh. The Phillies then ran themselves out of a chance to add an insurance run in the eighth inning. Turner led off with an infield single and Bryce Harper walked. Turner was then picked off stealing third by Martin, but Harper advanced from first to third on a wild pitch to the backstop. After Luis Arraez grounded out, Harper tried to steal home and was originally ruled safe by home plate umpire Dan Merzel. However, the call was overturned following a lengthy replay challenge by the Angels. Los Angeles then tied it, 1-1, in the bottom of the eighth on Neto's 23rd home run, a 407-foot drive to left-center on the 12th pitch of the at-bat off reliever Jonathan Bowlan. The Phillies took a 2-1 lead in the 10th on Schwarber's bloop double, driving in J.T. Realmuto, who had reached on a fielder's choice and advanced to third on Justin Crawford's single. Turner followed with a two-run single to right, scoring pinch runner Garrett Stubbs and Crawford. Los Angeles produced one run in the bottom of the inning on a fielder's choice by Wade Meckler, driving in automatic runner Denzer Guzman. Philadelphia starter Cristopher Sanchez was denied a major league-leading 17th win despite allowing just two hits over seven shutout innings. The left-hander walked one and struck out eight to give him 202 strikeouts for the season, the second straight season he has struck out at least 200 batters. Sanchez also extended his road scoreless streak to 19 innings and became the third pitcher in Phillies history to have three consecutive road starts of six-plus shutout innings, joining Hall of Famer Steve Carlton (1981) and Cliff Lee (2011). --Field Level Media

item.title: One dead, several injured, in Swiss shooting incident, police say
item.description: A shooting in northern Switzerland has killed one person and injured at least five, some of them seriously, local police said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A shooting in northern Switzerland has killed one person and injured at least five, some of them seriously, local police said on Sunday. Cantonal police in Aargau said a manhunt is underway and they appealed to the public for any film or pictures of the incident, which the mass-market Blick tabloid said had occurred at a rave party in the hippodrome. A video on its site recorded successive gunshots being fired. Large areas of the Aarau town are cordoned off, police said, and it has increased its presence beyond the town as a precaution. Switzerland has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in Europe although violent shootings are rare and it approved tighter gun control rules in 2019.

item.title: Europe's central bankers fear more turbulence in testy U.S. relations
item.description: Europe's central bankers are leaving an annual getaway with their U.S. counterparts far from reassured that long-standing norms in global cooperation remain intact and worried that more turmoil is ahead for an already testy relationship with Washington, sources familiar with the discussion said.
item.dc:creator: Balazs Koranyi, Howard Schneider, Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: Europe's central bankers are leaving an annual getaway with their U.S. counterparts far from reassured that long-standing norms in global cooperation remain intact and worried that more turmoil is ahead for an already testy relationship with Washington, sources familiar with the discussion said. Federal Reserve policymakers went out of their way to ease their counterparts' concerns this week, promising to honor all of their commitments. But, given the separation between the central bank and the administration, they could offer no guarantees against sudden policy shifts by President Donald Trump, more than half a dozen officials on the sidelines of the Kansas City Fed’s annual Jackson Hole Economic Symposium said. Recent U.S. Treasury interventions to [USN:L6N43Y004 TEXT:"prop up the Japanese yen"] and to [USN:L1N44G0GD TEXT:"lower longer-term U.S. borrowing costs"] were particularly concerning as they foreshadowed more intervention and breaks with norms, the officials, who asked not to be named, said. After the August 1 yen transaction, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed that the Treasury had sold euros for the Japanese currency and said he reassured central banks in the region that the move was "just a [USN:S0N435009 TEXT:"reallocation of resources"]." On Friday, he said that the foreign exchange assets to buy yen came from the Treasury's [USN:L4N44Q02B TEXT:"Exchange Stabilization Fund"]. But European officials were especially annoyed the U.S. did not give them a customary heads-up that euro sales were part of the transaction, the sources said. "That was infuriating," one of them said. "You always pick up the phone and give heads-up." "The message to me is that the U.S. does whatever it wants." Others were more forgiving and said the transaction was so unusual that it may have been an honest oversight. Spokespeople for the European Central Bank and the Federal Reserve declined to comment. A U.S. official said the U.S.-Japan intervention was undertaken to counter disorderly movements in the yen and to support stability in global financial markets. "It was not directed at anyone else," the official said. "Treasury maintains close and ongoing communication with our international counterparts, but we do not comment on the operational details of those discussions." DEBT BUYBACK CONCERNS The sources also said that Bessent’s plan to increase buybacks of longer-dated bonds -- transactions that may need to be financed by issuance of more shorter-term maturities -- was also a concern to European central bankers because, like the yen purchase, it indicates the administration was willing to take unusual measures to cap borrowing costs. "These interventions normally offer just temporary relief," a second source said. "But they are clearly worried. So what is next? Will they put pressure on the Fed to start buying bonds on the market?" While the Fed is the sole U.S. monetary policymaking body, independent in that mission by design from the elected administration, the sources said Trump has shown he is willing to go to extraordinary lengths to get his will across. Their concern was that this could then set off upheaval in markets that would go far beyond the U.S. The U.S. official responded by repeating earlier statements that the increased long-end bond buybacks were aimed at providing greater liquidity in longer-dated sectors where Treasury gets high-quality buyback offers. "They are not monetary policy or an effort to impose a cap on interest rates," the official said. On Thursday, however, a U.S. Treasury official had told reporters the Treasury was "really focused on bringing those long-end yields lower" because they had risen above what the department viewed as "fair value." SWAP LINES AT RISK? Another of the Europeans' worries was that political meddling could eventually involve the dollar liquidity backstops provided by the Fed to the world's biggest central banks, considered a cornerstone of global financial stability, some of the sources said. These swap lines ensure that commercial banks around the world retain their access to U.S. dollars, especially in moments of financial stress. The Fed renews this facility year after year on the premise that it actually safeguards U.S. interests and markets, since overseas banks in moments of global market upheaval could otherwise be forced to dump U.S. bonds. "But rationality doesn't always prevail with this administration," a third source said. "When they run retaliatory trade policies with their closest allies, Trump could just say, 'Hey, they're ripping us off' and the swap lines could be gone overnight." The sources said there has not been even a hint that these backstops are in danger, and they still expected them to remain unchanged. The swap lines are authorized by the Federal Open Market Committee itself and operated exclusively by the Fed, not the administration. "Decisions concerning Federal Reserve facilities and swap-line arrangements rest with the Federal Reserve," the Treasury official said. "Nothing Treasury has announced regarding either yen operations or debt buybacks suggests otherwise." The official added that Bessent looked forward to discussing financial stability issues with G20 [USN:L1N44O1AV TEXT:"finance ministers and central bank governors"] in the coming days in Asheville, North Carolina, seeking to further press the administration's agenda on isolating Iran, fostering growth and reducing global imbalances. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh travelled to Europe just over a month into his job and went out of his way to foster good relations with officials there, leaving a predominantly positive impression, the sources said. In his debut Jackson Hole conference as Fed leader, he also posed for a customary photo with Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem, a small but still notable gesture since Trump is now engaged in an escalating and bitter trade war with Canada.

item.title: Swiatek encouraged by recent progress after toughest season of career
item.description: Six-times Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek said recent progress had encouraged her after what she described as the toughest season of her career as the Pole bids for her first major title of the year at the U.S. Open.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Six-times Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek said recent progress had encouraged her after what she described as the toughest season of her career as the Pole bids for her first major title of the year at the U.S. Open. The 25-year-old endured an unusually difficult first half of the campaign by her lofty standards. She reached the [USN:L1N3YT03L TEXT:"Australian Open quarterfinals"] before losing to eventual champion Elena Rybakina, fell in the [USN:L1N42802H TEXT:"fourth round at Roland Garros"], where she had previously excelled, and exited [USN:L8N43605J TEXT:"Wimbledon in the third round"] as she failed to defend her title. Swiatek, who has slipped to eighth in the world rankings, captured her first title of the season earlier this month with a commanding victory over Rybakina in the [USN:L6N44B019 TEXT:"Canadian Open final"], providing a timely confidence boost ahead of the year's final Grand Slam. After winning her maiden major title at Roland Garros in 2020, Swiatek has lifted at least one Grand Slam trophy in every season since 2022 and will be eager to preserve that streak. "For me, for sure, it wasn't an easy season," Swiatek said on Saturday. "Probably the toughest one and the most challenging. "Obviously, I had to change coaches before the clay court season, which was a tricky situation. Then I started working with Francis ([USN:L4N40L121 TEXT:"Francisco Roig"]), and just wanted to implement all the stuff that we did in practice. "But, on the other hand, I didn't have a lot of practice time. So probably it calmed down, everything calmed down after Wimbledon. I managed to get some days off, reset a little bit, and we had a much longer training block. So it really helped me to just implement this stuff that I was talking about." Swiatek said recent results had left her encouraged by the progress she has made. "The last two tournaments (Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open) were super positive," she said. "Even though I lost in Cincinnati, this [USN:L6N44J07F TEXT:"match against Jess"] (Jessica Pegula in the semifinals) was really high level. "So I feel happy with my game and with the changes that I made. Just looking forward now." The former world number one can also draw confidence from her record in New York, where she claimed the U.S. Open title in 2022. She has not advanced beyond the quarterfinals at Flushing Meadows since, however, exiting at that stage in each of the last two years. Swiatek opens her U.S. Open campaign against China's Wang Xiyu. The men's and women's singles main draws get under way later on Sunday.

item.title: Islande-Une courte majorité défavorable aux discussions d'adhésion à l'UE, le décompte se poursuit
item.description: Une courte majorité d'électeurs islandais s'oppose à la reprise des négociations d'adhésion à l'Union européenne (UE), selon les résultats préliminaires du référendum organisé à ce sujet relayés dimanche par la chaîne de télévision publique RUV.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une courte majorité d'électeurs islandais s'oppose à la reprise des négociations d'adhésion à l'Union européenne (UE), selon les résultats préliminaires du [USN:L6N44Q009 TEXT:"référendum"] organisé à ce sujet relayés dimanche par la chaîne de télévision publique RUV. Après le dépouillement de 152.000 bulletins, 50,1% des électeurs sont défavorables à la proposition du gouvernement de relancer les négociations, tandis que 49,9% se sont prononcé pour cette proposition, a rapporté RUV. Aucune information concernant la participation au scrutin n'était disponible, alors que 270.000 personnes sont inscrites sur les listes électorales en Islande. Un résultat définitif pourrait n'intervenir qu'en milieu de journée dimanche, ont des responsables des élections. Les bureaux de vote ont fermé leurs portes à 22h00 GMT samedi. Une victoire du "oui" serait bien accueillie à Bruxelles, certains responsables estimant que l'Islande présente peu de risque et que la position géographique de l'île est attractive alors que la question de la sécurité dans l'Arctique prend de plus en plus d'importance. VOIR AUSSI: LE POINT sur le référendum en Islande sur les négociations d'adhésion à l'UE. ([USN:L8N44P0SC TEXT:"Full Story"])

item.title: Rain delays in Milwaukee create two-race Sunday
item.description: An unrelenting rain system led to a red flag on lap 90 of the Snap-On Makers and Fixers 250 in Milwaukee Saturday, and the cars couldn't return to the track.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An unrelenting rain system led to a red flag on lap 90 of the Snap-On Makers and Fixers 250 in Milwaukee Saturday, and the cars couldn't return to the track. Instead, the race is now scheduled to resume at 9 a.m. ET Sunday with the final 160 laps or end at 10:25 a.m. ET, whichever comes first. The delay will now create a double-header -- the Snap-On Milwaukee Mile 250 will follow directly after the first race. Pato O'Ward of Arrow McLaren holds the lead at the break. Felix Rosenqvist is in second, while Alexander Rossi is in third. This is the second time a race has been postponed a day this season. The Music City Grand Prix outside of Nashville suffered the same fate in July. --Field Level Media

item.title: Inondations-La Chine a identifié les pays d'origine de 261 étrangers portés disparus
item.description: La Chine a annoncé dimanche que 261 ressortissants étrangers originaires de 23 pays étaient portés disparus du côté tibétain de la frontière avec le Népal à la suite de la coulée de boue dévastatrice qui a fait des centaines de morts et ravagé la région cette semaine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Chine a annoncé dimanche que 261 ressortissants étrangers originaires de 23 pays étaient portés disparus du côté tibétain de la frontière avec le Népal à la suite de la coulée de boue dévastatrice qui a fait des centaines de morts et ravagé la région cette semaine. Le bilan des crues soudaines qui ont frappé mercredi la région himalayenne entre le Népal et le Tibet chinois est désormais de 16 morts côté tibétain. Des responsables régionaux ont indiqué que 104 Népalais, 49 Indiens, 33 Lettons, 18 Américains et 15 Britanniques étaient portés disparus. Ils ont précisé que les autorités de Pékin avaient informé les missions diplomatiques étrangères. Ce décompte par nationalité est le premier communiqué par la Chine depuis [USN:L8N44N0I6 TEXT:"l'effondrement glaciaire"] qui a déclenché un torrent de glace, de roches, de boue et de débris dans les rivières himalayennes. Les autorités ont indiqué que 16 personnes avaient trouvé la mort dans le comté de Gyirong, au Tibet, samedi soir et que 546 autres étaient portées disparues. Au Népal, les services chargés de la gestion des catastrophes ont indiqué qu'au moins 675 personnes étaient mortes de ce côté de la frontière, que 2.498 étaient portées disparues et que 7.514 avaient été secourues. LA CHINE FAIT LE LIEN AVEC LE RÉCHAUFFEMENT CLIMATIQUE CCTV a rapporté dimanche que la catastrophe avait été "provoquée par l'instabilité des glaciers sous l'effet à long terme du réchauffement climatique", ajoutant qu'il s'agissait d'une "particularité nouvelle et marquante des catastrophes liées à la cryosphère" sur le plateau tibétain. Il a fallu six à sept minutes pour que la coulée de boue venue du côté népalais atteigne le comté de Gyirong, a rapporté CCTV, citant les conclusions de scientifiques chinois. Des images de vidéosurveillance filmées à la frontière montraient des torrents d'eau et de débris engloutissant des bâtiments tandis que des personnes tentaient de fuir. Le ministre chinois des Affaires étrangères, Wang Yi, a déclaré samedi à son homologue népalais lors d'un appel téléphonique que la coulée de boue constituait la "catastrophe transfrontalière la plus grave" de ces dernières années, et que les opérations de sauvetage présentaient une difficulté et une complexité sans précédent, selon CCTV. La Chine a mobilisé plus de 2.100 secouristes et alloué au moins 220 millions de yuans (28,2 millions d'euros) pour soutenir les efforts de secours. Pékin fournit également au Népal une aide financière d'urgence, des équipements de secours, des données satellitaires et hydrologiques, et a dépêché des experts en sauvetage dans les tunnels, a indiqué la chaîne de télévision. Les deux pays collaborent pour identifier les personnes disparus, quelle que soit leur nationalité, et renforcent leur coopération en matière de prévention et de gestion des catastrophes, ainsi que de lutte contre le changement climatique, a rapporté CCTV.

item.title: Nepal-Tibet death toll 750 from Himalayan flood, 3,000 missing
item.description: The death toll in Nepal and Tibet from last week's catastrophic floods hit 750 on Sunday with 3,044 missing, authorities said, while rescuers moved to higher ground as rain swelled river levels.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The death toll in Nepal and Tibet from last week's catastrophic floods hit 750 on Sunday with 3,044 missing, authorities said, while rescuers moved to higher ground as rain swelled river levels. Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-China border by a mudslide from [USN:L4N44N173 TEXT:"Wednesday's glacier collapse"] could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into rivers in Nepal. The Red Cross estimates that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change. China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Nepalese counterpart in a Saturday telephone call that the mudslide was their "most severe cross-border disaster" in recent years and that rescue operations were of unprecedented difficulty and complexity, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported. TUNNELS BECOME A FOCUS OF RESCUE EFFORTS Nepal's rescue effort is now focused on hundreds of people believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower plants after a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris crashed down Himalayan rivers. Deaths in Nepal have risen to 734, with 2,498 missing and 7,514 rescued, the nation's disaster authority said. In China, 16 people had died in Gyirong County as of Saturday evening and 546 were missing, officials in Tibet told a press conference. Among the 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries missing on the Tibetan side were 104 from Nepal, 49 from neighbouring India, as well as 33 Latvians, 18 Americans and 15 Britons, they said in China's first breakdown by nationality. Beijing and Kathmandu are working together to identify missing citizens and foreign nationals, as well as strengthening cooperation in disaster prevention and mitigation, and climate-change response, CCTV said. Water levels in the Trishuli River rose on Sunday after fresh rain, prompting residents and rescue workers to seek higher ground, Nepalese police told Reuters. Nepal says it does not need foreign help for general rescue, but Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said the country needed assistance in such areas as tunnel rescue, DNA testing, refrigerated storage for bodies and forensic identification of decomposed remains. Indian and Chinese experts are on the ground helping efforts to open tunnels, Chhetri said. The lake that had formed upstream and threatened rescue operations had largely drained by Saturday evening, CCTV said. But drones detected a landslide late on Saturday 2.8 km (1.7 miles) downstream of the lake, forming a new dam and a fresh pool of water, CCTV said. The authorities relocated rescue personnel near the Gyirong border crossing to safety, the broadcaster said. LINK TO 'LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE' The flood was "caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming", CCTV reported, saying it was a "new and prominent feature of cryosphere disasters" on the Tibetan plateau. The mudslide from the Nepalese side took six to seven minutes to reach the Gyirong border crossing, CCTV said, citing the findings of Chinese scientists. Dramatic surveillance footage shared worldwide showed torrents of water and debris engulfing buildings while people tried to flee. China has mobilised over 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least 220 million yuan ($32.7 million) to support relief efforts. It is also providing emergency cash aid, disaster relief supplies, satellite and hydrological data and tunnel rescue experts to Nepal, CCTV said. China used heavy-lift drones as helicopters began airdropping equipment and supplies to frontline rescuers near the border crossing. Soldiers have used life-detection equipment, drones and a navigation system to continue searching for those still missing.

item.title: América registra cuarto triunfo consecutivo y se consolida como líder invicto en torneo mexicano
item.description: América se consolidó el sábado como el líder invicto del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano al registrar su cuarto triunfo consecutivo tras vencer por 2-0 a Puebla en la sexta jornada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: América se consolidó el sábado como el líder invicto del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano al registrar su cuarto triunfo consecutivo tras vencer por 2-0 a Puebla en la sexta jornada. Las "Águilas" del América llegaron a 16 puntos en lo más alto de la tabla general después de cinco victorias y un empate. Lo escoltan Tijuana con 13 unidades y Atlas con 12. "Hay que mantener los pies sobre la tierra, seguir con la misma humildad y saber que hay cosas que hay que mejorar, pero muy satisfecho por la entrega y el fútbol que están demostrando porque es la línea en la que debemos continuar", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico del América, el uruguayo Guillermo Almada. "Nuestros rivales han dejado puntos y nosotros hemos tenido la virtud de lograr triunfos continuos. Independientemente de quien sea el rival hay que seguir con la propuesta e intentar ganar todos los partidos", agregó. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, América estuvo cerca de anotar el primer gol a los 18 minutos con un disparo de Diego Arriaga que pegó en el travesaño. El equipo local se puso en ventaja a los 24 minutos cuando el brasileño Ícaro Da Conceição definió con un potente disparo desde fuera del área. América estuvo cerca de anotar el segundo gol a los 36 minutos con un remate de cabeza de Alejandro Cárdenas que pegó en el poste izquierdo tras un desvío del portero Ricardo Gutiérrez. Cuando Puebla jugaba mejor, el uruguayo Brian Rodríguez anotó el segundo gol a los 77 minutos con un disparo en la entrada del área tras recorrer desde el sector izquierdo hacia el centro del área. En otros partidos del sábado, Querétaro venció por 3-1 como visitante al Atlas con doblete del uruguayo Santiago Homenchenko y otro tanto del español Carlo García, quien anotó el tanto para los "Rojinegros" del Atlas al meter el balón a su propia portería al desviar un remate. Pachuca y Guadalajara empataron por 1-1 con goles del venezolano Salomón Rondón y Roberto Alvarado, respectivamente. En tanto, Santos Laguna y Tigres UANL empataron sin goles. La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Toluca juegue ante Bravos de Ciudad Juárez y Monterrey enfrente al Atlético de San Luis. El viernes, el campeón Cruz Azul puso fin a una racha de tres derrotas consecutivas al golear por 3-1 como visitante a Necaxa, Tijuana venció por 2-0 a Pumas UNAM, mientras que Atlante y León empataron 1-1.

item.title: Australia's far-right party makes further gains, taking seat in western state
item.description: Australia's far-right One Nation party won a seat in a state parliament long held by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's centre-left Labor Party, continuing a surge that had gained the populist group its first seat in the national lower house.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's far-right One Nation party won a seat in a state parliament long held by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's centre-left Labor Party, continuing a surge that had gained the populist group its first seat in the national lower house. Gym owner Luke Herdegen scored One Nation's first lower house seat in the Western Australia parliament, an official tally showed on Sunday, taking a seat in the state capital Perth that had been held by Labor for decades. One Nation, led by Senator Pauline Hanson, overtook Labor in a national opinion [USN:L1N42902Z TEXT:"poll"] for the first time in June, a month after [USN:L1N41M023 TEXT:"winning"] its first elected seat in the federal House of Representatives. Founded in 1997, One Nation long occupied the political fringe, but its hard line on immigration has drawn more support amid public frustration over housing shortages, high living costs and a general decline in support for Australia's major parties. The result underscores the challenge One Nation poses to Australia's main centre-left and centre-right parties as it converts rising poll numbers into seats, raising the stakes ahead of an election in Victoria state later this year. Tanya Plibersek, a senior federal Labor minister, said in televised remarks that Herdegen's win meant her party should "think about what more we need to do to communicate the fact that the Labor Party is the only party focused on real delivery to take pressure off ordinary Australians". Herdegen said late on Saturday that his win in the Perth suburb of Secret Harbour represented a "huge message" to Labor in Western Australia and nationally. "It sends a message that there are no safe Labor seats in this state or in this country," he said in remarks broadcast by News24. Herdegen beat a Labor newcomer with 57% of the vote in the by-election after longtime incumbent Paul Papalia resigned, citing a family medical issue. The constituency, which changed boundaries and names over the years, had been held by Labor since 1989.

item.title: Vélez Sarsfield empata con Deportivo Riestra en liga argentina
item.description: Vélez Sarsfield igualó el sábado 1-1 en su visita a Deportivo Riestra y alcanzó la cima de la Zona A en la séptima jornada del torneo Clausura del fútbol argentino.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vélez Sarsfield igualó el sábado 1-1 en su visita a Deportivo Riestra y alcanzó la cima de la Zona A en la séptima jornada del torneo Clausura del fútbol argentino. Con la igualada, Vélez se ubicó líder junto con Instituto de Córdoba con 13 puntos, uno por encima de Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza. En el partido disputado en el estadio Guillermo Laza, Riestra abrió el marcador a los nueve minutos con un remate de cabeza de Tomás González, mientras que Vélez Sarsfield igualó a los 76 a través de Matías Pellegrini. El conjunto dirigido por Guillermo Barros Schelotto llegó al segundo gol a los 85 minutos por intermedio de Manuel Lanzini, pero el árbitro Nazareno Arasa lo anuló a instancias del VAR. "El árbitro y el VAR tienen la responsabilidad de que Vélez no haya ganado el partido. Es un día triste, no tienen que dirigir nunca más a Vélez", dijo Barros Schelotto en rueda de prensa. Por su parte, Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata venció 2-1 en su visita a Rosario Central con goles de Ignacio Fernández e Ignacio Miramón en el estadio Gigante de Arroyito. El empate transitorio del conjunto local lo anotó el colombiano Jáminton Campaz. "No fue nuestro mejor partido, no es el nivel que veníamos mostrando, con dinámica y confianza", dijo el director técnico de Rosario Central, Jorge Almirón. En otros partidos del sábado, Huracán empató 1-1 como local ante Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, mientras que los encuentros entre Atlético Tucumán-Belgrano y Talleres-Central Córdoba finalizaron sin goles. La jornada inició el viernes con el triunfo por 1-0 de Boca Juniors ante Lanús y la goleada por 4-1 de Unión de Santa Fe sobre Sarmiento de Junín.

item.title: Parry defeats Mertens in Monterrey to claim maiden WTA singles title
item.description: France's Diane Parry stayed resilient to defeat Belgian second seed Elise Mertens 6-4 0-6 6-3 in the Monterrey Open final on Saturday, securing her maiden WTA singles title in her final tune-up ahead of the U.S. Open.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France's Diane Parry stayed resilient to defeat Belgian second seed Elise Mertens 6-4 0-6 6-3 in the Monterrey Open final on Saturday, securing her maiden WTA singles title in her final tune-up ahead of the U.S. Open. Parry, 23, took control of the match early at the WTA 500 event, racing to a 4-1 lead in the opening set before 30-year-old Mertens stormed back to level. Parry won the next game and then broke Mertens to take the first set 6-4. But a dominant Mertens emerged for the second set as the Belgian won six straight games, breaking her opponent three times. Parry took a medical timeout while down 5-0 in the second set but returned to the match. The Frenchwoman found her momentum again in the deciding set, taking a commanding 5-1 lead before the Belgian started inching her way back, winning back-to-back games. But a resilient Parry served out the set 6-3 to win her first Tour-level singles title in just over two and half hours. Parry will face Swiss Viktorija Golubic at the U.S. Open on Monday.

item.title: South Korea names veteran technocrat Lee Hyoung-il as new finance chief in cabinet reshuffle
item.description: South Korea unveiled a major cabinet reshuffle on Sunday, naming First Vice Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il as the new deputy prime minister and minister of economy and finance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea unveiled a major cabinet reshuffle on Sunday, naming First Vice Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il as the new deputy prime minister and minister of economy and finance. The administration also tapped ruling Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Seung-won to lead the Ministry of Justice, and named Kang Shin-chul, former deputy commander of the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command, as the new defense minister, presidential chief of staff Kang Hoon-sik said in a televised address. The reshuffle of the cabinet comes as President Lee Jae Myung's administration seeks to revitalize its international policy momentum as it enters its second year, at a time when analysts are questioning the sustainability of his expansionary fiscal policies amid a rout in the local bond market. Lee Hyoung-il, a career technocrat who has held the vice finance minister position since June last year, inherits an economy running hotter than expected and will be working with a central bank that is now tightening policy as the government is expected to boost fiscal spending for the year ahead. The government is expected to roll out its 2027 budget next week. In South Korea, cabinet nominees must face strict legislative scrutiny before they can formally be appointed by the president. The president retains the ultimate constitutional authority to appoint his ministers, even if parliament votes them down.

item.title: Michael Block continues hot play, grabs lead at Ally Challenge
item.description: Michael Block ripped an eagle on his opening hole and kept the pressure on Saturday, finishing 7-under-par 65 to grab a two-stroke lead at the Ally Challenge in Grand Blanc, Mich.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Block ripped an eagle on his opening hole and kept the pressure on Saturday, finishing 7-under-par 65 to grab a two-stroke lead at the Ally Challenge in Grand Blanc, Mich. Block, perhaps most well known for his top-15 finish at the 2023 PGA Championship, is in pursuit of his first win on the PGA Tour Champions circuit, fresh off a top-five showing last week at the Rogers Charity Classic, another high mark in his career. Competing on a sponsor exemption, Block knows that continuing to string together strong finishes is doubly important for him. "Top-10 is huge for me," Block said. "If I get a top-10, it gets me into the Sanford International in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, which has been a huge goal of mine because if I do get that, it will be my seventh start and that would officially put me into the official Charles Schwab Cup money list, which would get me into the Playoffs, which would get me then into Norwood Hills and St. Louis, which is where I'm from ... so there's a lot going on." His eagle on the par-5, 563-yard No. 1 provided a splash, but following his big round that left him at 13 under, Block was quick to credit the steadying influence of his son, Ethan, who serves as his caddie. "Great round, consistent round," Block said. "My son Ethan, who's on the bag, is the level-headed human out of my family. It's a Godsend that he's on my bag because I'm the least level-headed human being in the world. Glad to have Ethan on the bag, he got me through it." Block's steady play at Warwick Hills was notable, resulting in a bogey-free round. He added birdies on Holes 5, 7, 9, 13 and 16. To secure his first win, Block will have to hold off a field that includes Rogers-winner and current holder of second-place Steven Alker of New Zealand. Alker shot a 7-under 65 to match Block, going bogey-free with seven birdies to get to 11 under. "It was nice. I felt comfortable out there," Alker said, acknowledging his momentum. "Just start building, start feeling better with my shots, starting to drive it a little bit better. Everything just feels like it's getting a little bit better." Ireland's Padraig Harrington is three back at 10 under after carding 69. He's alone in third place. Argentina's Ricardo Gonzalez (69) and Vaughn Taylor (72) are tied for fourth at 9 under. Four more golfers are tided for sixth at 8 under: Thailand's Thongchai Jaidee (65), Argentina's Angel Cabrera (68), Chad Campbell (68) and Australia's Greg Chalmers (69). --Field Level Media

item.title: L'accord énergétique entre le Venezuela et les USA est d'une durée de 25 ans
item.description: La présidente par intérim du Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, a déclaré samedi que l'accord énergétique conclu entre Caracas et Washington resterait en vigueur pendant 25 ans.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La présidente par intérim du Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, a déclaré samedi que l'accord énergétique conclu entre Caracas et Washington resterait en vigueur pendant 25 ans. Une hausse de la production de pétrole, portant le nombre de barils produit chaque jour à 1,5 million, est prévue par le texte, a-t-elle dit, ajoutant que l'accord préservait la souveraineté du Venezuela sur ses ressources naturelles. Dans une allocution, Delcy Rodriguez a déclaré que cet accord "historique" aiderait à relancer l'économie du pays et à stimuler les recettes du gouvernement, estimant qu'il permettrait d'écrire le futur du pays.

item.title: Venezuela's interim president says US energy deal will last 25 years
item.description: Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday that an energy agreement with the U.S. would remain in force for 25 years, target an increase in crude output to 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and preserve the country's sovereignty over its natural resources.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday that an energy agreement with the [USN:FWN44P1ZC TEXT:"U.S."] would remain in force for 25 years, target an increase in crude output to 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and preserve the country's sovereignty over its natural resources. Rodriguez hailed the accord in a late-night address as a "historic" deal that would help revive the economy and boost government revenue, saying it would help shape the country's future. “This 25-year bilateral project envisages the development of 17 strategic oilfields with a production target of more than 1.5 million barrels per day," Rodriguez said on state broadcaster VTV. "That figure relates solely to the bilateral agreement between Venezuela and the United States." Rodriguez added that the agreement's target of 1.5 million bpd was only an initial goal and that the broader plan also included the development of eight greenfield oil blocks as part of a wider expansion of the country's energy sector. President Donald Trump on Friday announced plans for the U.S. to take partial control of Venezuela's vast oil reserves, betting that American companies can help revive the South American nation's battered energy industry while providing a new source of crude to help lower U.S. fuel prices. Trump provided few details on the agreement, saying only that the U.S. had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business. Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves, but it produces only about 1.25 million bpd - far below its potential - after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions. Rodriguez said the agreement could generate about $209 billion in revenue for the Venezuelan state, based on a benchmark oil price of $65 per barrel, though she acknowledged crude prices could fluctuate. She said roughly $19 from each barrel produced and sold under the arrangement would flow directly to Venezuela, providing a significant boost to government revenue. She said that the country retained “ownership of and sovereignty” over its natural resources, “while leveraging capital, technology and operational expertise to support the recovery of a strategic industry that has been severely affected by sanctions." Earlier on Saturday, dozens of pro-government groups gathered in downtown Caracas to protest against the U.S. presence in Venezuela. Rodriguez welcomed the agreement following Trump's announcement, saying it would bolster economic growth and increase government revenue. Venezuelan officials are preparing to sign agreements next week granting new oil exploration and production rights to several companies, including U.S. firms. Two sources close to the negotiations said on Friday that [USN:L6N44P13H TEXT:"Chevron CVX.N was among the companies"] expected to finalize talks to transition its Venezuelan joint ventures into the country's new energy framework.

item.title: Presidenta encargada de Venezuela dice que acuerdo petrolero con EEUU será por 25 años
item.description: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, dijo el sábado que el acuerdo petrolero con Estados Unidos se mantendrá vigente durante 25 años con el objetivo de aumentar inicialmente la producción de crudo a 1,5 millones de barriles diarios, agregando que el país sudamericano mantiene la soberanía sobre sus recursos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, dijo el sábado que el acuerdo petrolero con Estados Unidos se mantendrá vigente durante 25 años con el objetivo de aumentar inicialmente la producción de crudo a 1,5 millones de barriles diarios, agregando que el país sudamericano mantiene la soberanía sobre sus recursos. Rodríguez elogió el acuerdo con Washington en un discurso transmitido por la televisión estatal en horas de la noche y lo calificó de "histórico", porque reactivará la economía y aumentará los ingresos del gobierno. "Este proyecto binacional, suscrito por 25 años, contempla el desarrollo de 17 campos estratégicos con un objetivo de producción superior a 1,5 millones de barriles diarios. Esto solamente con el acuerdo binacional Venezuela-Estados Unidos, pero nuestra meta va más allá", agregó Rodríguez, quien señaló que el proyecto contempla el desarrollo de ocho campos verdes (greenfields) en la Faja del Orinoco. El viernes, el presidente Donald Trump [USN:L6N44Q004 TEXT:"anunció"] planes para que Estados Unidos tome el control parcial de las vastas reservas petroleras de Venezuela, apostando a que las empresas estadounidenses pueden ayudar a reactivar la maltrecha industria energética del país miembro de la OPEP, a la vez que proporcionan una nueva fuente de crudo para ayudar a reducir los precios del combustible en Estados Unidos. Trump ofreció pocos detalles sobre el acuerdo, limitándose a decir que Estados Unidos había asegurado el control mayoritario de más de 65.000 millones de barriles de las reservas probadas de petróleo de Venezuela mediante una alianza con empresas privadas. "Tomando como referencia un precio de 65 dólares por barril (...) los ingresos de nuestro país llegarían a un total de 209.335 millones de dólares para el Estado venezolano. En términos concretos, esto significa que por cada barril producido y vendido cerca de 19 dólares ingresan directamente a nuestro país", añadió Rodríguez, sin más detalles. Venezuela posee las mayores reservas probadas de petróleo del mundo, pero produce solo alrededor de 1,25 millones de barriles diarios, muy por debajo de su potencial tras años de baja inversión, mala gestión y sanciones. Tras agradecer al presidente Trump y al secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, los esfuerzos por el acuerdo, la presidenta encargada dijo que Venezuela mantiene la soberanía sobre sus recursos naturales. "Venezuela conserva la propiedad y la soberanía sobre sus recursos, mientras utiliza capital, tecnología y capacidad operativa para apalancar la recuperación de una industria estratégica duramente golpeada por sanciones", añadió. Funcionarios venezolanos se preparan para firmar la próxima semana acuerdos que otorgarán nuevos derechos de exploración y producción de petróleo a varias empresas, en particular a firmas estadounidenses. Dos fuentes indicaron el viernes que [USN:L6N44P13Z TEXT:"Chevron"] figuraba entre las petroleras que finalizarían las negociaciones para integrar todas sus empresas mixtas en Venezuela al nuevo marco energético del país.

item.title: Brewers get early HRs, strong outing from Shane Drohan to top Rangers
item.description: Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning and Shane Drohan tossed five solid innings as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the visiting Texas Rangers 5-3 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning and Shane Drohan tossed five solid innings as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the visiting Texas Rangers 5-3 on Saturday. Drohan (7-5) allowed one run on six hits with one walk and six strikeouts for his first victory since July 31. Luis Lara had two hits and two RBIs for Milwaukee, which won its fourth straight. The Rangers trailed 5-1 with one out in the eighth inning before pulling closer on Brandon Nimmo's two-run homer against Chad Patrick. Antonio Senzatela replaced Patrick and allowed Ezequiel Duran's single before retiring the next two batters. Trevor Megill pitched a scoreless ninth for his 25th save. Cody Freeman hit a solo homer and Nimmo had three hits for Texas, which lost its fourth straight. Milwaukee claimed a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Cal Quantrill (6-5) on a pair of solo homers by Chourio and Contreras. Chourio's one-out shot over the center field wall was his third homer in his last three games and his 20th of the season. After Jake Bauers struck out, Contreras turned on Quantrill's 2-2 sinker for his 13th homer of the year. The Brewers tacked on a run in the second inning. Christian Yelich hit a leadoff double, stole third, and scored on Lara's liner into center field. Lara was thrown out on the play while attempting to stretch the single into a double. Texas got on the board when Freeman began the fifth inning with his first homer of the season. Quantrill was replaced by Peyton Gray after allowing three runs on four hits with no walks and a season-high eight strikeouts over six innings. He retired the final 14 batters he faced. Milwaukee extended its lead with two runs against Gray in the seventh. With the bases loaded and no outs, Lara singled in a run and another run scored on Cooper Pratt's sacrifice fly. The Brewers loaded the bases with two outs in the eighth, but Jakob Junis struck out Lara to escape the jam. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tyson Bagent, Bears blitz Titans, 24-15
item.description: Bears backup quarterback Tyson Bagent and wide receiver Zavion Thomas connected on a 97-yard touchdown on Chicago's opening play and didn't stop there in a 24-15 win over the Titans in Nashville on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bears backup quarterback Tyson Bagent and wide receiver Zavion Thomas connected on a 97-yard touchdown on Chicago's opening play and didn't stop there in a 24-15 win over the Titans in Nashville on Saturday. Thomas, a rookie third-round pick, made his preseason debut and racked up 140 yards on five receptions with a 39-yard punt return. Bagent was almost perfect as a passer -- he completed 16 of 17 throws for 208 yards and two touchdowns -- and the Bears (2-1) overcame his fumble on a busted run play in a game that featured mostly reserves in the closing preseason action for both clubs. On first down from their own 3, Bagent dropped back into the end zone and locked onto Thomas split wide to his right. Thomas hesitated and the Titans' secondary froze. With the pocket shrinking around him, Bagent let the ball go as Thomas, who was the third-fastest player timed at the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine, shifted gears. He came back for the underthrown pass, then burst into the open, sprinting down the sideline for the touchdown. Bears wide receiver Maurice Alexander caught Bagent's other TD toss and had a game-high seven receptions for 50 yards. The Bears led 14-9 at halftime. Chicago added Roschon Johnson's 3-yard touchdown run and a Cairo Santos field goal in the third quarter to push their lead to 24-9. Johnson had 15 carries for 52 yards. With starting quarterback Cam Ward and backup Mitch Trubisky rested, quarterback Will Levis, fighting for a roster spot ahead of NFL cuts, started for the Titans. He played the entire first half and led three scoring drives (all field goals). Running back D'Ernest Johnson scored Tennessee's only touchdown on a 9-yard run with 3:50 to play and celebrated with the "Choppa City Juke," an homage to former Titans running back Chris Johnson. Titans kicker Joey Slye made all three of his field goal tries, including a 56-yarder, his fifth this preseason of at least 50 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: US to take 35% stake in Venezuelan mogul Betancourt's oil venture, WSJ reports
item.description: The U.S. government plans to take a 35% passive stake in Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt’s North American Blue Energy Partners, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people involved in negotiating the deal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. government plans to take a 35% passive stake in Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt’s North American Blue Energy Partners, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people involved in negotiating the deal. The U.S. also plans to secure preferential rights to purchase 20% of the company's production at cost, the WSJ reported. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital plans to structure the investment through penny warrants that would yield the U.S. an equity ownership in the business without significant capital investment, the WSJ reported. The report comes only a day after U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday that the U.S. would take control of a [USN:FWN44P1ZC TEXT:"fifth"] of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. Trump provided few details about the arrangement, saying only that the U.S. had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business. Responding to a Reuters request for comment, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said: "The Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) does not take equity stakes in private companies. Under its statutory authority, OSC's role is strictly limited to providing capital assistance in the form of a loan, loan guarantee, or technical assistance (including transaction structuring for developing and financing investments)." The White House and North American Blue Energy Partners did not respond to requests for comments outside regular business hours.

item.title: President Donald Trump to attend Presidents Cup
item.description: President Donald Trump will serve as the honorary chairman at the 2026 Presidents Cup and plans to attend the event that will be held at Medinah Country Club in Chicago from Sept. 24-27.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump will serve as the honorary chairman at the 2026 Presidents Cup and plans to attend the event that will be held at Medinah Country Club in Chicago from Sept. 24-27. "At the request of the PGA Tour, and its Great new Commissioner, Brian Rolapp, it is my Honor to accept being the Honorary Chairman of the upcoming Presidents Cup, which will take place at the Medinah Country Club in Chicago," Trump said in a statement posted on Truth Social. "This will be a particularly exciting event. Both teams are "loaded" with Talent. I look forward to being there, and greeting all of these fantastic athletes, on both teams! Thank you for your attention to this matter. See you in Chicago! Trump served the same role for the 2017 Presidents Cup held at Liberty National Golf Club in New Jersey during his first presidential term. The U.S. won that competition over the international team, 19-11. He also made an appearance during the first round at last year's Ryder Cup held at Bethpage Black on Long Island. "The Presidents Cup has a proud tradition of engaging world leaders from across the globe and across political lines, and President Trump's involvement continues that legacy," PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said in a statement. "His participation will help elevate the event on the international stage while furthering our mission of bringing people together through the game of golf." Brandt Snedeker will serve as captain of the American team that will take on an international team led by captain Geoff Ogilvy of Australia next month. Trump joins six former presidents to serve as the honorary chairman for the event: Joe Biden, Barack Obama, George W. Bush, Bill Clinton, George H.W. Bush and Gerald Ford. Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau took part in the trophy presentation at the most recent Presidents Cup at Royal Montreal in 2024. Other world leaders who have held the position include Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison and South Korean President Park Geun-hye. --Field Level Media

item.title: Emotional Federer full of love and gratitude at Hall of Fame induction
item.description: An emotional Roger Federer said he was still writing his love letter to the sport that "meant the world" to him on Saturday as the 20-time Grand Slam champion was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An emotional Roger Federer said he was still writing his love letter to the sport that "meant the world" to him on Saturday as the 20-time Grand Slam champion was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island. Federer, who was inducted alongside broadcaster and journalist Mary Carillo, reflected on his storied career in a speech that brought him to tears a few times. "This is one of the greatest honours of my life," said Federer. "They call this the Hall of Fame, but fame was never the goal. "My goal was to spend my life doing something I love ... with people who love it as much as I do." The Swiss captured a men's-record eight Wimbledon titles and spent 310 weeks as the world number one. He also won six Australian Open crowns, five U.S. Open titles and one French Open title. And he did it all while playing with elegance, a signature headband – apparently wearing more than 5,000 of them during his career, he quipped in his address – and almost always two pairs of socks. "Tennis meant the world to me. Not just playing, not just winning, but creating something new," said Federer, who retired in 2022 with 103 ATP Tour titles. "It's a mentality I have. I used to play serve and volley, I had a transition game, I played way beyond the baseline sometimes, or on top of the baseline. And I would even try to sneak up on my opponents on my return, and some call it the SABR (Sneak Attack by Roger) today. "This is what was important to me on the court, but so much of what was really important happened off the court." The 45-year-old got emotional while thanking his coaches, doctors and family, including wife Mirka, who praised Federer for his character off the court as husband, father and friend. As his name entered the Hall of Fame, Federer said he was proud that Switzerland was coming with him, recalling how he loved watching tennis as a 13-year-old ball boy in Basel. "I'm still writing my love letter to tennis, and my time as a player is done, but tennis will always stand at the intersection of everything I care most about," he said. "My family, our friendships, the past 40 years, the future we're building – tennis, for me, is responsible for it all. So this is not a goodbye." The Swiss said he was "incredibly lucky" to have played with different generations of tennis players, from Andre Agassi and Lleyton Hewitt to Andy Roddick, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. But he added that his induction was not only an opportunity to look back on his career, but also ahead to the future of the game. "We all leave the court eventually, but the sport keeps evolving," said Federer. "And as the pace of professional tennis speeds up, as the sport becomes even more global, I so hope it will keep some of that amateur spirit. Keep the camaraderie among the players. "I hope the players will stay young at heart and stay true to their authentic selves, and always remember, never stop asking questions or taking risks. "Do things with the game, we've never seen before. Keep pushing this sport we love to the next level and keep getting better, better, and better."

item.title: Yankees SS George Lombard Jr. (knee) makes early exit vs. Red Sox
item.description: The New York Yankees removed rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. from the nightcap of their doubleheader with the visiting Boston Red Sox on Saturday night due to right knee discomfort.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Yankees removed rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. from the nightcap of their doubleheader with the visiting Boston Red Sox on Saturday night due to right knee discomfort. The team said Lombard was undergoing imaging at New York-Presbyterian Hospital. In the second inning, Lombard checked his swing on a pitch from Brayan Bello. Afterward, Lombard grimaced and held his right knee. After a team athletic trainer and manager Aaron Boone checked on him, Lombard stayed in the game and singled. Lombard batted in the third and flew out to left field after the Yankees took a 3-1 lead but was lifted for the start of the fourth inning. New York moved Jose Caballero from third base to shortstop and Amed Rosario entered the game at third. Lombard joined the team on Aug. 4 and was the first Yankees shortstop to homer in his major league debut. The 21-year-old is batting .253 with two homers and six RBIs in 23 games since getting promoted from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reports: Cowboys acquire Steelers '23 first-rounder Broderick Jones
item.description: Offensive tackle Broderick Jones is being acquired by the Dallas Cowboys, who agreed to a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Saturday that includes three 2027 draft picks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Offensive tackle Broderick Jones is being acquired by the Dallas Cowboys, who agreed to a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Saturday that includes three 2027 draft picks. ESPN reported the trade agreement in place, pending a physical, sends Jones and a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Cowboys for third- and sixth-round picks in 2027. Jones, the Steelers' first-round pick in 2023, made 38 starts over three years but was working with the reserves in Pittsburgh during the preseason. He played both tackle spots in Pittsburgh. The Steelers drafted Max Iheanachor at No. 21 overall in April to play right tackle. He has been competing there with fifth-year veteran Dylan Cook while 2024 first-round pick Troy Fautanu has worked at left tackle. Former Cowboys coach Mike McCarthy, familiar with that organization's preference for a well-stocked offensive line, is entering his first season as Steelers coach. Terence Steele was the primary right tackle for the Cowboys last season. Dallas has been pleased with 2024 first-round pick Tyler Guyton at left tackle in the preseason. If Jones winds up taking over at right tackle, Dallas could start four first-round picks around center Cooper Beebe. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Mets place OF Luis Robert Jr. on waivers
item.description: The New York Mets placed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. on waivers, per MLB.com.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Mets placed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. on waivers, per MLB.com. The former All-Star, who pinch-hit during the Mets' 6-2 win over the Houston Astros on Saturday, has posted 10 home runs and 23 RBIs with a .229/.308/.407 slash line in 57 games this season. Those numbers include a strong push in August as he has amassed six home runs and 11 RBIs with a .282/.338/.557 line over 23 games. His ability to play center field could make him appealing to contenders, as well. Robert was an All-Star in 2023 with the Chicago White Sox, blasting 38 home runs and stealing 20 bases. However, injuries and inconsistency have hampered his production and value. The 29-year-old is owed roughly $3 million for the rest of this season. He also carries a $20 million club option for next season, though there's a $2 million buyout. With the Mets out of playoff contention, it is not surprising to see them trying to shed some salary. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pajari heading for third win in a row
item.description: Toyota's Sami Pajari was heading for his third win in a row after ending the penultimate leg of Rally Paraguay with a 24.1-second lead on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Toyota's Sami Pajari was heading for his third win in a row after ending the penultimate leg of Rally Paraguay with a 24.1-second lead on Saturday. The Finn, winner in Estonia and Finland, had been 11.9 seconds clear of New Zealander Hayden Paddon at the start of the day and managed his tyres to stretch his advantage over the largely dry day's nine stages to move within five of victory. "For me this is a different challenge than Estonia and Finland," said Pajari, who lost part of his rear wing when he ran wide in stage 11. "It is more about surviving. Many things can go wrong still tomorrow." Hyundai's Paddon ended the day 32.2 seconds clear of Toyota's world championship leader Elfyn Evans with Hyundai's Adrien Fourmaux challenging for the podium in fourth after winning five stages and closing the gap to 3.3 seconds after starting Saturday 55 seconds behind. Welshman Evans said Fourmaux, a distant sixth in the standings, was able to take risks because he had less to lose than others. “Adrien, to be fair, has been in a different rally to everyone else,” he said. “He is risking everything, but let’s see tomorrow.” Evans leads Pajari by 30 points in the standings with three rounds remaining after Paraguay.

item.title: Ethiopian Gobena and Kenya's Jepchirchir take Sydney marathon honours
item.description: Gobena crossed the line at the city's Opera House in two hours, four minutes and 42 seconds.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ethiopian Addisu Gobena smashed the course record to win the men's title before Kenya's world and former Olympic champion Peres Jepchirchir dominated the women's race at the Sydney Marathon on the penultimate day of the Australian winter on Sunday. Gobena, second last year, crossed the line at the city's Opera House in two hours, four minutes and 42 seconds, well clear of the previous record of 2:06:06 that his compatriot Hailemaryam Kiros clocked to win the race last year. Chimdessa Debele of Ethiopia was second in 2:04:46 with Lesotho’s Tebello Ramakongoana third in 2:04:57. “I am very happy," said 21-year-old Gobena, who broke clear of the five-strong leading pack in the closing stages to record the fastest-ever marathon time on Australian soil. "Last year I came second, I learnt from my mistake, and I went back home and I worked on my mistake to perform and broke the record today.” Jepchirchir blew away the field in the women's race, finishing more than three minutes clear of second-placed compatriot Irine Cheptai in 2:18:31 to win her fourth marathon major. Cheptai ran a time of 2:22:11 in perfect running conditions, while Ethiopian Shure Demise was third in 2:22:33. The 32-year-old Jepchirchir, who won Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021, came up just short of the course record of 2:18:22 that current Olympic champion Sifan Hassan ran to win the Sydney race last year.

item.title: Michael Harris II's clutch double enables Braves to drop Rockies
item.description: Michael Harris II laced a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth inning on Saturday to help the streaking Atlanta Braves earn a 2-1 victory over the visiting Colorado Rockies.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Harris II laced a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth inning on Saturday to help the streaking Atlanta Braves earn a 2-1 victory over the visiting Colorado Rockies. Atlanta mounted a two-out rally in the eighth. Colorado reliever Jaden Hill (0-3) allowed singles by Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubon before Harris split the left-center gap with the Braves' lone extra-base hit. Didier Fuentes handled the ninth for the Braves. After issuing a leadoff walk to Willi Castro and allowing a one-out single to Troy Johnston, the 21-year-old Fuentes struck out Zac Veen and got Jake McCarthy to line out to seal his third save and Atlanta's sixth straight win. Brent Suter (2-2) threw 2 1/3 scoreless innings for the Braves. Colorado's Ryan Feltner was scratched from his scheduled start due to illness.
